tools.name: New device setup (full build chain)
tools.description: Primary user, McAfee removal, debloat, M365 Apps, Chrome + Reader and vendor drivers, then an HTML build report.
brief: The whole new-laptop build in one pass: Intune primary user (if given) > McAfee removal >
OEM debloat > M365 Apps reinstall > Chrome + Reader > Dell / HP / Lenovo drivers.
Ends with an HTML build report: each step and its result, outstanding Windows and driver
updates, device details and app versions. Setting a user? Sign in at the start, then leave it.
tools.confirm: Runs the full build (20-40 min) and REBOOTS the machine at the end.

prompts.prompt: Ticket number for the build report (optional)
Your name for the build report (blank = this Windows account)
Intune primary user to set: their sign-in address (blank = leave as is)
Or remove the Intune primary user (shared device)?
Skip the Dell / HP / Lenovo driver updates?
Skip the automatic reboot at the end?

tools.name: McAfee removal
tools.description: Strips Store, MSI and EXE McAfee preloads. Exit 3010 = removed, reboot.
brief: Removes the McAfee that Dell ships: the Store app, the MSI parts and WebAdvisor / LiveSafe.
Silent. Log in C:\ProgramData\McAfeeRemoval.
Changes the machine: uninstalls McAfee only.

tools.name: OEM debloat (HP / Dell)
tools.description: Removes OEM and consumer bloat, keeps SupportAssist / HP Support Assistant.
brief: Strips HP / Dell consumer bloat and Windows consumer apps from a fresh build.
Keeps the useful OEM tools (SupportAssist, HP Support Assistant, hotkey and system drivers).
Changes the machine. Pick dry run below to see what would go without removing anything.

prompts.prompt: Dry run only (log what would go, change nothing)?
Force silent uninstall of EXE apps with no known silent switch?

tools.name: OEM drivers + BIOS (Dell / HP / Lenovo)
tools.description: Scans with the vendor's own updater (Dell Command Update, HP Image Assistant, Lenovo LSUClient), lists, asks, installs. Never restarts.
brief: Works out if it's a Dell, HP or Lenovo and uses that vendor's own updater.
Scans and lists driver and firmware updates, then asks again before installing anything.
Asks first if it needs to install the vendor's updater. Never restarts the machine.
BIOS only if you say yes below - plug the charger in for that.

prompts.prompt: Include BIOS updates (plug the charger in)?

tools.name: M365 Apps reset + reinstall
tools.description: ODT removal of every Office install, optional Microsoft Get Help deep scrub, then a clean M365 Apps install.
brief: Removes every Office install (OEM stubs, language packs, old MSI Office), then reinstalls
a clean Microsoft 365 Apps from Microsoft (about 3-4 GB, 10-20 minutes).
Deep clean adds Microsoft's Get Help Office scrub for broken installs.
Restart afterwards, then sign in to Office to activate.
tools.confirm: Removes ALL installed Office and reinstalls (3-4 GB download).

prompts.prompt: Licence type
Also run Microsoft's Get Help deep scrub (slower, for broken installs)?

tools.name: Chrome + Adobe Reader install
tools.description: Chrome Enterprise MSI + offline Reader, with Reader cloud/AI features locked down.
brief: Downloads and silently installs the latest Google Chrome (Enterprise MSI) and Adobe Reader
64-bit, with Adobe's cloud, AI Assistant and upsell bits switched off.
Installs software only; nothing is removed.
Each installer must be validly signed by Google or Adobe, or it's deleted and not installed.

prompts.prompt: Install which

tools.name: Intune primary user (change or remove)
tools.description: Shows, changes or removes this PC's Intune primary user (and Entra owner), signed in as a tenant admin.
brief: Signs in to this PC's Microsoft 365 tenant as an admin (Microsoft's sign-in window, MFA works).
Shows the PC's Intune primary user, then sets the user you give, or removes it (shared device).
Intune updates the Entra device owner to match. Changes the tenant, not this PC.
Needs Intune Administrator or Help Desk Operator. Leave the address blank to just look.

prompts.prompt: New primary user's sign-in address (blank = just show the current one)
Remove the primary user instead (shared device)?

tools.name: Driver export (before a wipe)
tools.description: Backs up every third-party driver with a manifest and restore note.
brief: Backs up every third-party driver on this machine before a wipe, with a list of what was
saved, the machine's details and the one command that puts them back.
Only copies drivers out - changes nothing on this machine. Optional zip for the USB stick.

prompts.prompt: Export folder (blank = C:\DriverExport\<PC>_<model>_<date>)
Zip it into one file as well?

tools.name: Driver import (from an export)
tools.description: Installs every driver from a previous export folder or .zip with pnputil.
brief: Installs every driver from an earlier driver export (folder or .zip) using pnputil.
Drivers already on the machine are skipped.
Changes the machine: installs drivers. A restart may be needed afterwards.

prompts.prompt: Export folder or .zip to install from

tools.name: Windows repair checks (DISM + SFC)
tools.description: DISM RestoreHealth, SFC /scannow, DISM component cleanup.
brief: Repairs Windows system files: DISM RestoreHealth, then SFC, then DISM component cleanup.
Can take 20+ minutes. Stops at the first failure and shows which step.
The cleanup step makes installed updates permanent (they can't be uninstalled after).
Ends with CHECKS COMPLETE - PLEASE RESTART SYSTEM.

tools.name: Windows Update reset
tools.description: Stops update services, sets aside SoftwareDistribution and catroot2, restarts, rescans.
brief: Fixes stuck or failing Windows Updates: stops the update services, renames the download
cache and catalog (kept, not deleted), starts everything again and kicks off a fresh scan.
Checks for the usual culprits first (pending reboot, WSUS policy, low disk).
tools.confirm: Renames SoftwareDistribution and catroot2. Update history in Settings starts empty (installed updates stay).

prompts.prompt: Also reset Winsock (only if updates fail to download at all; needs reboot)?
Delete .old copies left by previous resets?

tools.name: Teams cache clear (new + classic)
tools.description: Closes Teams, empties the cache folder Microsoft documents (settings kept), starts Teams again. Run as the user.
brief: Clears the Teams cache for the signed-in user, then starts Teams again.
First fix for Teams being slow, blank, stuck signing in or showing old names and photos.
Settings survive. Run it as the user, not as admin.

prompts.prompt: Leave Teams closed afterwards?

tools.name: Print spooler clear
tools.description: Stops the spooler, deletes stuck jobs (.SPL/.SHD only), starts it again with its dependants.
brief: Clears stuck print jobs: stops the Print Spooler, deletes the queued jobs, starts it again.
Shows how many jobs are queued first. Printers, drivers and settings aren't touched.
tools.confirm: Deletes every queued print job on this PC - people will need to print again.

tools.name: Office activation reset
tools.description: Microsoft Get Help ResetOfficeActivation: clears Office licences and cached sign-ins so the user can activate fresh.
brief: Resets Office activation with Microsoft's Get Help: clears Office licences and signs Office
out of its cached accounts, so the user can sign in and activate fresh.
For 'Unlicensed Product', the wrong account, or activation trouble after a licence change.
tools.confirm: Closes all Office apps and signs Office out. The user signs in again afterwards.

tools.name: Teams Meeting add-in fix (classic Outlook)
tools.description: Checks the add-in is installed and registered; fixes LoadBehavior, Outlook's disabled list and do-not-disable list. Run as the user.
brief: Fixes the missing Teams Meeting button in classic Outlook for the signed-in user.
Checks the add-in is installed and registered, and fixes the Outlook settings that hide it.
Run it as the user, not as admin. Check-only mode changes nothing.
tools.confirm: Closes classic Outlook if it needs to fix anything.

prompts.prompt: Check only (change nothing, leave Outlook open)?

tools.name: OneDrive reset (sync app)
tools.description: Microsoft's OneDrive.exe /reset for the signed-in user: finds the right OneDrive.exe, lists accounts and synced libraries, resets, then makes sure OneDrive starts again. Run as the user.
brief: Microsoft's OneDrive reset (OneDrive.exe /reset) for the signed-in user, then starts it again.
For sync that's stuck, errors that keep coming back, or files that never upload.
Disconnects every OneDrive account here and re-syncs; no files are deleted.
Lists accounts and synced libraries first. Run it as the user, not as admin.
tools.confirm: Signs this user's OneDrive out of every account until it re-syncs. Files stay put.

prompts.prompt: Check only (show accounts and synced libraries, change nothing)?

tools.name: Quick triage (first five minutes)
tools.description: Device, uptime, reboot, disk, crashes, updates, AV, Entra/Intune and network on one page, problems first. Optional Wi-Fi + battery reports.
brief: The first five minutes of a ticket on one page: device, uptime, reboot, disk, crashes,
updates, antivirus, Entra / Intune and network - problems first, each with a next step.
Read-only. Ends with a one-line summary to paste into the ticket.

prompts.prompt: Write the one-page HTML report too?
Also save Windows' Wi-Fi + battery reports (Wi-Fi needs admin)?

tools.name: Performance check (slow PC)
tools.description: Why is it slow? Measures CPU, disk and memory for 30 seconds, names the apps responsible, and checks power settings, startup apps, hangs, SSD vs hard drive and RAM. -Fix offers undoable fixes, one question at a time.
brief: Why is it slow? Measures the PC for 30 seconds - ask the user to do what's slow meanwhile -
then names the apps using CPU, memory and disk, and checks power settings, startup apps,
hangs, start-up time, SSD or hard drive, and RAM. Each problem comes with what to do.
Read-only by default. Say yes below to be offered fixes you can undo, one at a time.
Run as admin to see start-up times. Never restarts.

prompts.prompt: Write the one-page HTML report too?
Offer fixes afterwards (power plan, startup apps), asking before each one?

tools.name: Before / after comparison
tools.description: Reads the Quick triage, Performance check, Wi-Fi and battery reports saved for this PC and writes up what changed: fixed, worse, the numbers side by side, what's left and what to look at next.
brief: Before and after on one page. Reads the Quick triage, Performance check, Wi-Fi and battery
reports already in C:\Triage for this PC, then shows what got fixed or worse, the numbers
side by side, what's still to do, and things that only show when the reports are read together.
Read-only: writes one HTML page next to the reports. Run the checks before and after first.

prompts.prompt: Ticket number for the report (optional)

tools.name: Entra / Intune health check
tools.description: Join state, PRT, MDM enrolment, certs, last check-in, IME, event errors, endpoints.
brief: Checks the Entra join, SSO token, Intune enrolment, check-ins, agent and certificates.
Says what's wrong in plain English, with a fix for each.
Read-only, unless you choose a sync or a log bundle below.

prompts.prompt: Trigger an Intune sync after the checks (needs admin)?
Bundle logs into a zip for escalation (needs admin)?

tools.name: BitLocker key backup check
tools.description: Is every recovery key backed up to Entra? Event 845/846 per key; -Fix backs up the missing ones. Never shows the keys.
brief: Checks every BitLocker recovery key on this machine has actually reached Entra ID.
Read-only, unless you say yes below to backing up the missing ones.
The recovery keys themselves are never shown.

prompts.prompt: Back up any keys that aren't proven backed up to Entra?

tools.name: Device inventory (hardware + OS)
tools.description: Model, serial, RAM sticks, disks and wear, monitors, battery, network, TPM.
brief: One-page hardware and OS summary: model, serial, CPU, RAM sticks, disks and their health,
monitors with serials, battery wear, network and security state.
Read-only.

prompts.prompt: Write an HTML report as well?

tools.name: Disk usage report (HTML)
tools.description: TreeSize-style scan: biggest folders, files and safe cleanup targets.
brief: Finds what's eating the disk: biggest folders, biggest files and known cleanup targets.
Writes an HTML report you can attach to the ticket. Read-only - deletes nothing.

prompts.prompt: Path to scan (blank = system drive)

tools.name: Disk usage browser (GUI)
tools.description: Live folder-size browser. Look, don't touch: it can't delete anything.
brief: Opens a TreeSize-style window to browse folder and file sizes.
Browse only - there's no delete anywhere.

tools.name: Event triage (GUI)
tools.description: Groups event log noise into what's actually wrong. Local or remote.
brief: Opens a window that groups the event logs into problems, worst first, with known noise
hidden. Works on this machine or a remote one.
Read-only. Run elevated to include the Security log.

tools.name: M365 licence report (Excel)
tools.description: Graph-based user + licence workbook with reclaim and unlicensed sheets.
brief: Signs in to a tenant (Microsoft Graph) and writes an Excel report of every user and their
licences, with optional last sign-in and stale-account flags.
Read-only in the tenant. Signs out when done. Installs modules only if ticked below.

prompts.prompt: Tenant ID or domain (blank = pick at sign-in)
Client name for the filename (blank = tenant name)
Include last sign-in (needs AuditLog.Read.All)?
Install missing Graph / ImportExcel modules?

tools.name: Exchange + Planner usage report
tools.description: Who is licensed for Exchange / Planner but not using it. CSV + Excel.
brief: Per-user Exchange and Planner usage for a tenant: who's licensed but not using them.
Signs in to the tenant, writes a CSV (and Excel if ImportExcel is installed).
Read-only, except: if the tenant hides names in usage reports, it asks to show them
for this run and hides them again afterwards.

prompts.prompt: Tenant domain, e.g. contoso.onmicrosoft.com
Connect via GDAP (partner access)?
Skip the Planner sign-in log scan (faster on big tenants)?
